User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the music library application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

Rental.title: Rental
Rental.description: Represents a rented instrument by a user.

instrumentName.description: The name of the rented instrument.

issueDate.description: The date the instrument was issued.

returnDate.description: The expected return date of the instrument.

definition.description: Stores user profiles. Users can only access their own profile. Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence. userId MUST match request.auth.uid.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user. Must match request.auth.uid.

definition.description: Stores a user's instrument rentals. A user can only access their own rentals.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user. Must match request.auth.uid.

params.name: rentalId
params.description: The unique identifier of the rental.

firestore.reasoning: This design prioritizes simplicity and security for user authentication and data ownership. It directly reflects the provided entities and focuses on path-based ownership. The `users/{userId}` collection stores user profiles. The `users/{userId}/rentals` subcollection stores instrument rentals. Authorization is straightforward: users can only access their own documents in their respective `/users/{userId}` trees. This is enforced through path-based rules, eliminating the need for complex `get()` calls and ensuring Authorization Independence. QAPs are inherently supported as `list` operations are restricted to a user's own data.
